title: A test that a value function ignores units

blocks.text: A transit agency's analysts keep rewriting the function that values its projects. Before any new version is used, the agency wants an automatic check that the version does not care what units the data arrived in: if every measure and its reference are restated in other units (hours to minutes, dollars to thousands of dollars), the projects must come out in the same order.

items: `ranking(values)`: the project names from the highest value to the lowest. Values closer than `TIED` count as equal, and equal values are listed in name order. Near-ties **chain**: walk down the names sorted by value, and put each one in the same tied group as the name just before it when the two values are within `TIED`. So three values each within `TIED` of the next form one group, listed in name order, even if the first and the last are further apart. Floating-point arithmetic rounds: two values that are equal on paper can differ in their last digit, and in the other direction once the units change. Rounding alone must never make the check fail.

`survives_rescaling(value, benefits, reference, factors)`: `value(benefit, reference)` is the function under test, `benefits[project]` maps each measure to an amount, and `factors[measure]` is how many new units one old unit is. Restate every amount and every reference, rank the projects before and after, and return whether the two rankings are the same.

blocks.text: The tests pass in a normalized value function, which must pass the check, and a raw sum, which must fail it. About fifteen lines.

cases.says: a ranking lists names from the highest value down, equal values in name order
a normalized value function passes the check and a raw sum, whose first place moves, fails it
a raw sum whose first place holds but whose lower places swap still fails the check
two values equal but for floating-point rounding are a tie, so rounding alone never fails the check
values each within TIED of the next form one tied group, even when the ends are further apart
